svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.10.15.3 Limiting Distance and Fire Department Response
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.15.3 Limiting Distance and Fire Department Response
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Limiting Distance and Fire Department Response

g.text: WHEN HALF THE LIMITING DISTANCE IS USED
More than 10 min in 10% or more of all calls to the building
And any storey in the building is not sprinklered

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
A limiting distance equal to half the actual
limiting distance is used as input to the
requirements of this Subsection, where
(a) the time from receipt of notification of a
fire by the fire department until the first fire
department vehicle arrives at the building
exceeds 10 min in 10% or more of all calls to the
building, and (b) any storey in the building is
not sprinklered. Except for the purpose of
and 9.10.15.5.(13). See Notes A-3.2.3. and
Only the time from receipt of notification of a
fire by the fire department until the first fire
department vehicle arrives at the building is
considered. The 10-min limit must be met in more
than 90% of the calls to the building,
essentially consistent with NFPA 1710.
Note A-3.2.3.
Code provisions against fire spread from building
to building use the limiting distance rather than
the distance between adjacent buildings, so that
the design of a building on one property does not
affect the design of a building on an adjacent
property.
Drawn: a 2 storey house with no sprinklers, 4 m from the property line. Red dashed: the property line.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.15.3. (page 9-88)
